trace_issues.name: WS-PROC-IX
trace_issues.message: WS-PROC-IX is declared by INDEXED BY on WS-PROC-ENTRY (line 56, field SYS-PORTFOLIO-001-FIL-0046-FLD-000008 occurs.indexed_by). It is an index name, not a data item, and has no Field ID: not looked up, recorded as resolution INDEX_NAME with target_id null, not counted as unresolved. It keeps its role as the table subscript set by SET (lines 158, 185).

The read loop ends only when WS-PSR-STATUS = '10' (set by the AT END branch at line 171 or by the READ itself). A READ that fails with another status takes neither AT END nor NOT AT END, so the loop would repeat; no other status is tested inside the loop.
Loops at lines 207, 230 and 293 can end early through EXIT PERFORM (statements 107, 108, 113).
WS-PROC-IX is incremented once per matching sequence record without a check against the OCCURS 100 limit of WS-PROC-ENTRY.
Static CALL 'ERRPROC' USING ERR-MESSAGE in 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE; external program, not traced into.

program_narrative: PRCSEQ00 is a batch subprogram (PROCEDURE DIVISION USING LS-SEQUENCE-REQUEST, ends with GOBACK) that manages the run sequence of batch processes for a processing date. The caller selects one function per call: INIT opens PROCESS-SEQ-FILE and BATCH-CONTROL-FILE, positions the sequence file by the processing date, loads every sequence record of the requested sequence type into an in-memory process table with status READY, and writes one batch-control record per entry. NEXT finds the first READY entry in the table, reads its process definition, checks each dependency's batch-control record (a hard dependency that is not DONE sets return code BCT-RC-WARNING; a DONE dependency whose return code exceeds the allowed maximum sets BCT-RC-ERROR) and, if the return code is still zero, marks the process ACTIVE with a start time and rewrites its control record. STAT reads the control record of LS-NEXT-PROCESS, copies its status and return code into the table and counts active and error entries. TERM recounts, returns BCT-RC-ERROR if any entry is in error, BCT-RC-WARNING if any is still active, otherwise BCT-RC-SUCCESS, and closes both files. Error conditions handled: invalid function code, open and close failures, START/READ/WRITE/REWRITE invalid keys; each sets an error text and performs 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE, which sets BCT-RC-ERROR and calls ERRPROC, after which processing continues. The dependency subscript WS-SUB is not declared anywhere.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN
pseudocode: -- Entry point: dispatch on the function code passed by the caller in LS-SEQUENCE-REQUEST
SET RETURN-CODE = ls_return_code  -- RETURN-CODE special register: program return code seen by the caller
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Entry point: dispatch on the function code passed by the caller in LS-SEQUENCE-REQUEST
SELECT CASE function_code (LS-FUNCTION)
  WHEN 'INIT' (FUNC-INIT):
    CALL 1000-initialize-sequence
  WHEN 'NEXT' (FUNC-NEXT):
    CALL 2000-get-next-process
  WHEN 'STAT' (FUNC-STAT):
    CALL 3000-check-status
  WHEN 'TERM' (FUNC-TERM):
    CALL 4000-terminate-sequence
  ELSE:
    SET error_text = 'Invalid function code'
    CALL 9000-error-routine
END SELECT
SET RETURN-CODE = ls_return_code  -- RETURN-CODE special register: program return code seen by the caller
RETURN to caller  -- GOBACK

annotations.note: RETURN-CODE is a COBOL special register, not a data item; it is not looked up in the field registry.

SET ws_proc_ix = 1  -- WS-PROC-IX is the INDEXED BY index of the WS-PROC-ENTRY table (a table position, not a data item)
SET psr_key = ls_process_date  -- group move: the 8-character date fills the 10-byte key PSR-KEY (PSR-PROCESS-ID + PSR-VERSION), rest padded with spaces
POSITION PROCESS-SEQ-FILE at the first record with key >= psr_key  -- START KEY >=
IF no such record (INVALID KEY) THEN
SET error_text = 'No sequence found for date'
WHILE ws_psr_status != '10' DO  -- '10' = end of file
READ next record from PROCESS-SEQ-FILE into PROCESS-SEQUENCE-RECORD
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
CLEAR ws_process_table, ws_process_count  -- INITIALIZE: alphanumeric items to spaces, numeric items to zero
SET ws_proc_ix = 1  -- WS-PROC-IX is the INDEXED BY index of the WS-PROC-ENTRY table (a table position, not a data item)
SET psr_key = ls_process_date  -- group move: the 8-character date fills the 10-byte key PSR-KEY (PSR-PROCESS-ID + PSR-VERSION), rest padded with spaces
POSITION PROCESS-SEQ-FILE at the first record with key >= psr_key  -- START KEY >=
IF no such record (INVALID KEY) THEN
  SET error_text = 'No sequence found for date'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF
WHILE ws_psr_status != '10' DO  -- '10' = end of file
  READ next record from PROCESS-SEQ-FILE into PROCESS-SEQUENCE-RECORD
  IF end of file THEN
    SET ws_psr_status = '10'
  ELSE
    IF psr_type = ls_sequence_type THEN
      CALL 1210-add-to-sequence
    END IF
  END IF
END WHILE

paragraphs.name: 2210-CHECK-DEP-STATUS
pseudocode: READ record from BATCH-CONTROL-FILE where key = bct_key  -- random READ by RECORD KEY BCT-KEY (job name, process date, sequence no)
IF record not found (INVALID KEY) THEN
IF dependency is not done (BCT-STATUS != 'D') THEN
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
SET bct_job_name = psr_dep_id[ws_sub]
SET bct_process_date = ls_process_date
READ record from BATCH-CONTROL-FILE where key = bct_key  -- random READ by RECORD KEY BCT-KEY (job name, process date, sequence no)
IF record not found (INVALID KEY) THEN
  SET error_text = 'Dependency record not found'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF
IF dependency is not done (BCT-STATUS != 'D') THEN
  IF dependency is hard (PSR-DEP-TYPE[ws_sub] = 'H') THEN
    SET ls_return_code = bct_rc_warning  -- +4
  END IF
ELSE
  IF bct_return_code > psr_dep_rc[ws_sub] THEN
    SET ls_return_code = bct_rc_error  -- +8
  END IF
END IF

annotations.note: BCT-SEQUENCE-NO (third part of BCT-KEY) is not set before the keyed READ; it keeps the value left in the record area.
BCT-STATUS-DONE is the 88-level BCT-STATUS = 'D'; PSR-DEP-HARD is the 88-level PSR-DEP-TYPE = 'H' (subscripted by the undeclared WS-SUB).
